full_judgment: 6. The learned Advocate Md. Nurul Hoque for the opposite party submitted that there is no bar to add party in a pre-emption case at any stage of the case and the appellate court decided for sending the case back on remand only because pre-emption of a bonafide pre-emptor cannot be refused. In support of the above contention he referred to a case reported in 31 D.L.R. (AD)-88 (Akhtarun Nessa and another Vs. Habibullah and other) where-in their lordships held. It is the requirement of the statute that all the co-sharer tenants of the holding and all the tenants holding lands contiguous to the land transferred and the transferee shall be made parties, but a case of pre-emption under section 96 may not be defeated on the analogy of non-joinder of all co-sharer in a suit for partition. The reason is obvious, because, in .a suit for partition non-joinder of a co-sharer may prove fatal to the suit. But position in a pre-emption case is different. Right of pre-emption accrues on a transfer of a portion or share of holding of a raiyat or when a holding is transferred which gives rise to an application for pre-emption either under the first part or second part of sub-section (10) of section 96. This right is not absolute but subject to the right of other co-sharers and holders of land contiguous to the land transferred, as the case may be, requirement of the statue of imp leading has in who favour right of pre-emption accrued is for the sole purpose of enabling the court to adjudicate the claim of all the par-ties having right to pre-empt according to the provision under section (5) of section 90 in one proceeding and avoiding multiplicity of proceedings., So, for the sake of full and complete adjudication of the rights and granting relief, there should not be absence of any necessary party. In this instant case the opposite party No. I knew about the defect of parties at the time of trial before the learned Assistant judge but he did not take any step at that time to make them as party to the case and then proceeded with the case. Even no prayer for amendment was made before the trial court during the trial of the case. In a case reported in 1984 B.L.D. (AD)-27 (Jalaluddin Fakir Vs. Shahjahan Ali Molla and others) their lordships hold the view, which was also held in 33 D.L.R. (AD) 113, which is as follows." 33 DLR? (AD) 113 has laid down the law regarding necessary parties in a pre-emption application under sec-tion 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. There is has been held-"The right of pre-emption as provided under sub-section (1) of section 96 is a statutory right.. The cause of action, for pre-emption of any transfer accrues to the Co-sharer tenants and contiguous land owners. The right of the applicant of applicants claiming to be co-sharer tenants of owner of contiguous land, is not absolute but subject to the right of other Co-sharers and other holders of land contiguous to the land transferred as the case may be for proper adjudication. To give full effect to the statutory provision, all the necessary parties must be impleaded because relief cannot be given in the absence of such party."
